messages.content:
Convert the reference list below into a JSON array of 8 objects with keys authors (string), first_author_surname, year (integer or null), title, journal, doi (string or null; without https://doi.org/). Copy values exactly as written; do not correct anything. Output only the JSON.

Here are 8 peer-reviewed papers on text-message reminders for medication adherence. **Important caveat:** I'm providing these from memory, so citation details (especially DOIs) may contain errors—please verify each in PubMed or Google Scholar before citing.

1. **Vervloet, M., Linn, A. J., van Weert, J. C. M., de Bakker, D. H., Bouvy, M. L., & van Dijk, L. (2012).** "The effectiveness of interventions using electronic reminders to improve adherence to chronic medication: A systematic review of the literature." *Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association*. DOI: 10.1136/amiajnl-2011-000748

2. **Thakkar, J., Kurup, R., Laba, T. L., et al. (2016).** "Mobile telephone text messaging for medication adherence in chronic disease: A meta-analysis." *JAMA Internal Medicine*, 176(3), 340–349. DOI: 10.1001/jamainternmed.2015.7667

3. **Pop-Eleches, C., Thirumurthy, H., Habyarimana, J. P., et al. (2011).** "Mobile phone technologies improve adherence to antiretroviral treatment in a resource-limited setting: A randomized controlled trial of text message reminders." *AIDS*, 25(6), 825–834. DOI: 10.1097/QAD.0b013e32834380c1

4. **Lester, R. T., Ritvo, P., Mills, E. J., et al. (2010).** "Effects of a mobile phone short message service on antiretroviral treatment adherence in Kenya (WelTel Kenya1): A randomised trial." *The Lancet*, 376(9755), 1838–1845. DOI: 10.1016/S0140-6736(10)61997-6

5. **Mbuagbaw, L., van den Koppele, K. L., Ongolo-Zogo, P., et al. (2012).** "The Cameroon Mobile Phone SMS (CAMPS) trial: A randomized trial of text messaging versus usual care for adherence to antiretroviral therapy." *JAIDS Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes*, 60(2), e29–e32. DOI: 10.1097/QAI.0b013e318252d34b

6. **Wald, D. S., Butt, S., & Bestwick, J. P. (2014).** "One-way versus two-way text messaging on improving medication adherence: Meta-analysis of randomized trials." *American Journal of Medicine*, 127(9), 881–885. DOI: 10.1016/j.amjmed.2014.05.021

7. **Kannry, J., et al. / alternatively: Buis, L. R., Hirzel, L., Turske, S. A., Des Jardins, T. R., Yarandi, H., & Bondurant, P. (2017).** "Use of a text messaging platform to enhance adherence to weight loss behaviors in a diverse, low-income population." *JMIR mHealth and uHealth*, 5(2), e22. DOI: 10.2196/mhealth.6709

8. **Fisher, J. D., Fisher, W. A., Amico, K. R., & Harman, J. J. (2006)** — this is the Information-Motivation-Behavioral Skills model paper, not text messaging specifically, so a better fit: **DeKoekkoek, T., Given, B., Given, C. W., & Spoelstra, S. L. (2015).** "mHealth SMS text messaging interventions and to promote medication adherence: An integrative review." *JMIR mHealth and uHealth*, 3(3), e72. DOI: 10.2196/mhealth.4395

**Recommendation:** Search PubMed with terms like "text message reminder medication adherence" and filter for RCTs or systematic reviews to confirm exact details. The Pop-Eleches, Lester, Thakkar, and Vervloet papers are among the most highly cited in this field and are good starting points.
